extracted.intended_audience: State and Federally-facilitated Exchange operators, QHP issuers, web-brokers, agents/brokers, and HHS/CMS administrators
extracted.subtask_short: ACA Exchange operational and compliance standards
extracted.subtask_description: Operational, legal, and technical requirements for operating Health Insurance Marketplaces and entities that enroll consumers in QHPs, including website/display rules, enrollment pathways, civil rights compliance, partner vetting, timelines, and data protection obligations. Covers federal regulatory citations and related CMS/HHS guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exchange website requirement for standardized comparative information
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1311(d)(4)(C) of the Affordable Care Act requires the Exchanges to maintain an internet website through which enrollees and prospective enrollees of qualified health plans may obtain standardized comparative information on such plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory requirement to provide standardized comparative information online; see accompanying regulatory provisions implementing display detail (e.g., 45 CFR 155.205(b)).

rubrics_metrics.name: QHP comparative information display standard (§45 CFR 155.205(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: 45 CFR 155.205(b)(1) outlines the QHP comparative information which must be displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Websites (including issuers' and web-brokers' sites when used to complete selection) must differentially display all standardized options prominently and in accordance with the requirements under §155.205(b)(1) in a manner consistent with that adopted by HHS for display on the FFE website, unless HHS approves a deviation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility and single-site enrollment availability (§155.205(c) requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be at least one website available in the State that satisfies all accessibility requirements under §155.205(c), and at least one website through which consumers can view and enroll in all available QHPs in the State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consumer access and that accessibility standards are met within each State; addresses both accessibility and comprehensive enrollment capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Civil rights and nondiscrimination obligations for covered entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities such as States, recipients of Federal financial assistance from HHS, programs or activities administered by HHS (including the FFE), and entities established under Title I (such as State Exchanges) must comply with Federal civil rights laws prohibiting discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, and disability (including Section 1557, Title VI, Section 504, and the ADA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes the 2024 Section 1557 final rule expansion (and notes that portions have been enjoined); entities must follow applicable civil rights law and stay aware of litigation/enforcement status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enrollment-through-Exchange interpretation for issuer and web-broker enrollments
rubrics_metrics.description: For individuals to be eligible to receive PTCs, the Affordable Care Act requires enrollment in a QHP through an Exchange; HHS interprets this to allow a QHP issuer or a web-broker to enroll an applicant directly on their website and be considered enrolled 'through an Exchange' so long as the issuer or web-broker meets applicable requirements (§156.1230; §155.220(a)(2) and (c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enables direct enrollment via issuers or approved web-brokers when they comply with Exchange requirements; see related provisions for operational and contractual compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting and approval of Classic DE and EDE partners
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS, in coordination with third-party auditors, vets prospective Classic DE and EDE partners that want to operate on the FFE's DE or EDE pathway to ensure compliance with §§155.220 and 155.221 and meet other operational requirements; HHS maintains and publicly posts an updated list of approved DE and EDE partners.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HHS provides audit guidelines and decommissioning FAQs (links cited). Approved partner lists are posted on CMS websites; prospective partners must satisfy audit and operational criteria before operating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agent/broker/web-broker licensing and immediate-termination exception
rubrics_metrics.description: An exception allows immediate termination of the agent, broker, or web-broker's Exchange agreement(s) for cause without any further opportunity to resolve the matter upon providing notice where the agent, broker, or web-broker fails to maintain the appropriate license under applicable State law(s) (see 45 CFR 155.220(g)(3)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most other situations, termination follows other procedures; this is a limited situation focused on licensing noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of personally identifiable information (PII) by agents/brokers/web-brokers
rubrics_metrics.description: The agent, broker, or web-broker must continue to protect any PII accessed during the term of their Exchange agreements (see 45 CFR 155.220(g)(4) and 155.260).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PII protection obligations survive during the agreement term and are subject to cited regulatory privacy/security requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of CMS Model Consent Form and consumer consent requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS has an HHS‑approved and created CMS Model Consent Form for Marketplace Agents, Brokers, Web-brokers, and Agencies; CMS also provides FAQs on Consumer Consent & Application Review Requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market participants are directed to use the CMS model consent form and follow CMS FAQs for consumer consent and application review practices (links provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: State Exchange Blueprint change notification and approval
rubrics_metrics.description: A State must notify HHS and receive written approval from HHS before significant changes are made to the Exchange Blueprint; significant changes could include altering a key function of Exchange operations or other changes that impact operation (examples include the process for enrollment in a QHP).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This approach aligns with prior rulemaking (e.g., 77 FR 18316) and is intended to ensure HHS oversight of impactful operational changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: HHS review timeline for significant Exchange Blueprint change requests (§155.105(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS generally has 60 days after receipt of a completed request to complete its review of a significant change to an Exchange Blueprint and, for good cause, may extend the review period by an additional 30 days up to a total of 90 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States and Exchanges should plan for this statutory/regulatory review timeline when proposing significant operational changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for websites completing QHP selection to display standardized options consistently
rubrics_metrics.description: When an internet website of a web-broker or issuer is used to complete the QHP selection, at a minimum the internet website must differentially display all standardized options prominently and in accordance with the requirements under §155.205(b)(1) in a manner consistent with that adopted by HHS for display on the FFE website and with standards defined by HHS, unless HHS approves a deviation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures consistency in consumer-facing displays across platforms; deviations require HHS approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: State defrayal timing for State-mandated benefits included as EHB
rubrics_metrics.description: If the proposal is finalized as proposed, States would not be required to defray the costs of any State-mandated benefits that are included in the State's EHB-benchmark plan as EHB during PYs 2025-2026 but would be required to defray such costs beginning in PY 2027.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This describes a phased policy tied to Payment Notices and final rules; States should track applicable payment year responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'State-required benefits' as specific to care, treatment, or services
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS interprets 'State-required benefits' to include the care, treatment and services that an issuer must provide to its enrollees. Other State laws that do not relate to specific benefits, including those relating to providers and benefit delivery method, are not addressed in §155.170 (EHB Final Rule and 2017 Payment Notice citations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies scope of state-mandated benefit defrayal obligations; emphasizes narrow interpretation focused on specific benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS oversight review regarding defrayal of State mandated benefits (GAO recommendation response)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS concurred with the GAO's recommendation to review CMS' current oversight approach for defrayal of State mandated benefits and determine whether additional oversight is needed; work is ongoing (GAO-25-107220).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates active review and potential future changes to oversight practices; stakeholders should monitor CMS actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: AV (Actuarial Value) calculation methodology and bronze plan implications
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes finalized in the 2023 Payment Notice and subsequent AV Calculator improvements affect allowable AV ranges for plans (e.g., raising the lower bound of the permitted AV de minimis range from −4 percent to −2 percent so no bronze plans could be certified with an AV below 58 percent) and corrected prior underestimation for plans using 'copay with deductible.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why certain theoretical AVs no longer occur and describes the 'expanded bronze' definition (plans that cover/pay for at least one major service before the deductible or meet HDHP criteria). Stakeholders should use updated AV Calculator methodology and guidance documents cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network adequacy measurement factors (time and distance)
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS currently uses a calculation for network adequacy that factors in both time and distance. Time and distance is especially critical in large metro areas where there is a standard of 15 miles/30 minutes as an example.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Network adequacy determinations should consider both travel time and distance; example thresholds (e.g., 15 miles/30 minutes) illustrate standards in metro areas but may vary by context.
